reference_basis: +4 dBu is inside the published uniform de-essing range.
modeled_input: Main audio input of the de-esser module, modeled unbalanced with a 10 kΩ output load; external control-voltage connections are separate.
published_input_conditions: dbx specifies uniform de-essing from −40 to +24 dBu input without level readjustment, maximum input +24 dBu, 20 kΩ balanced or >10 kΩ unbalanced. Its 0–20 dB Range sets maximum attenuation, not input threshold.

reference_basis: Factory 0 VU meter alignment, +4 dB re 0.775 V. The meter trimmer can change hardware alignment.
modeled_input: Original mono 160 programme input; the model grounds the cold input and loads the output with 10 kΩ.
published_input_conditions: dbx factory-aligns 0 VU to +4 dB re 0.775 V RMS. Model 160 has 50 kΩ balanced or 25 kΩ unbalanced input, +21 dB (8.7 V RMS) maximum and a 10 mV–3 V threshold control. Specifications put the meter trimmer at −10 to +10 dB; the front-panel prose instead says −10 to +20 dB.

reference_basis: Factory -10 dBm bridging input. Default SW101A throw A feeds the wet section before R102/R103. Throw B adds the 10.1 dB divider for the 0 dBm input.
modeled_input: Unbalanced line insert into the Type B drive and tuned harmonics path, one engaged channel. A console send/return may also be used.
published_input_conditions: Aphex specifies switchable −10 or 0 dBm operation, a 47 kΩ bridging input, and +20 dBm maximum I/O. At the usual 600 Ω voltage reference these operating points are approximately 245 and 775 mV RMS.

reference_basis: Factory -10 dBu operating level at the 482i input.
modeled_input: Channel B unbalanced line input of the 482i for serial processing of a source, subgroup or stereo mix.
published_input_conditions: The 482i manual specifies −10 dBu operating level (245 mV RMS), 47 kΩ input, +18 dBu maximum input. Its output meter warns at +15 dBu, 3 dB below actual clipping; Lo Contour and Process can raise the output.

reference_basis: Provisional +4 dBu studio line input. Published high-output dBV levels refer to the opposite end of the unit.
modeled_input: One channel of the original line-level valve distortion unit. The hardware also has a front instrument/DI socket; this circuit reconstructs the line signal path.
published_input_conditions: The October 2005 manual lists 30 kΩ line input and places +4 dBV nominal and +17 dBV maximum at the high OUTPUT. It recommends 0.25–0.30 mA bias current for low distortion, and approximately 20 dB extra gain with Overdrive.

reference_basis: Provisional +4 dBu for the line input. The 550A’s +28 dBm rating is an output rating.
modeled_input: Early console 550A module, three proportional-Q bands with five frequencies per band and transformer output.
published_input_conditions: API’s original 15-frequency 550A sheet rates its transformer-coupled OUTPUT to +28 dBm. Studio Sound’s 1976 survey reports 0.07% THD at +18 dBm, without naming the port or termination; no exact-revision input nominal or limit was verified.

reference_basis: +4 dBu is inside the nominal range specified by API.
modeled_input: Ten-band 560 console/500-series line-EQ channel. The model estimates the gyrator cells and includes the transformer output.
published_input_conditions: The factory 560 sheet gives −15 to +15 dBu as the nominal level range, clipping above +28 dBu without specifying the port, and a separate +20 dBu OUTPUT distortion test. A +4 dBu program reference falls within the stated range.

reference_basis: Factory bandwidth test with 0 dBu input, EQ engaged and gains flat. Adopted as a repeatable Series II line-input reference.
modeled_input: Single channel of the Series II line-level parametric EQ, representing its bridging receiver and EQ stages.
published_input_conditions: 20 kΩ balanced bridging input; +26.8 dBu maximum input before clipping (0.1% THD+N). GML used 0 dBu (775 mV RMS), EQ in and bands flat for bandwidth testing, and +20 dBu for specified distortion tests.

reference_basis: Provisional 0 dBu internal EQ reference. Voltage at this specific board input is undocumented.
modeled_input: Internal equalizer and independent HP/LP filters from PC1003-A Rev 3. The source enters after the microphone/line input circuitry.
published_input_conditions: Harrison’s period desk technical-service figures, reprinted in Studio Sound, give +4 dB nominal and +24 dB maximum at the external line input, +6 dB nominal at patch points, and +24 dB maximum return, as printed. No operating figure at the isolated EQ input was established.

reference_basis: Provisional 0 dBu internal EQ reference. Voltage at this specific board input is undocumented.
modeled_input: Musicland Type 69 line EQ and 2128 makeup amplifier. The model omits the microphone transformer and preamp.
published_input_conditions: The Musicland desk drawings include several 0011 input-module revisions. The version with 2128 makeup documents the circuit. A nominal or clipping voltage at the modeled EQ feed was not found in the accessible documents.

reference_basis: Provisional professional 500-series line input. The output LED and headroom specification give separate overload checks.
modeled_input: Mäag EQ4-500 line EQ module. Its parallel bands sum, so an Air boost can also raise the overall output.
published_input_conditions: The original guide lists 48 kΩ balanced input, +25 dBu headroom (port unspecified) and an output peak LED starting at +23 dBu. It describes compensating the level rise from Air boost by lowering the five other controls together.

preset: Manley Massive Passive Standard Circuit Model
schematic_path: schematics/studio/eq/Manley Massive Passive Standard Circuit Model.livewdf
reference_basis: Published +4 dBu operating level at the modeled professional line input.
modeled_input: Original Standard rack EQ, one complete professional line channel including the input and estimated tube makeup stages.
published_input_conditions: The 1998–2004 manual specifies +4 dBu professional operation (1.228 V RMS). Quarter-inch input/output can switch internally to −10 dBV; the XLR stays at professional level. Original maximum INPUT is +20 dBm at 1.5% THD. The flat headroom/THD tests use +4 dBm as printed.

reference_basis: Original EB20031 drawing: -15 dBm at the internal filters, using the historical 0.775 V reference. The line input amplifier is absent.
modeled_input: Internal 1081 EQ feed at the input to the high/low-pass filters, after the sensitivity amplifier and before the four equalizer stages. The model omits the preamp, fader and line-output transformer.
published_input_conditions: Rupert Neve drawing EB20031 marks −15 dBm at the filter entrance and again between filter, presence and bass/treble sections. On the historical 0.775 V reference this corresponds to about 138 mV RMS. The separate rack trim procedure uses 0 dBu at 1 kHz at the external line XLR, unity sensitivity and output full clockwise.

reference_basis: +4 dBm on 600 ohms is explicitly recommended within the factory optimum-average range.
modeled_input: Original transformer-matched line program EQ, passive filter and tube makeup; preset uses an EQP-1A3 amplifier drawing.
published_input_conditions: For 600 Ω matching, Pulse Techniques gives −15 to +8 dBm optimum AVERAGE input and singles out +4 dBm as allowing room for peaks. Flat insertion gain is unity; the specification gives +21 dBm maximum OUTPUT and 0.15% distortion at +10 dBm into 600 Ω.

reference_basis: +4 dBm on 600 ohms is explicitly recommended within the factory optimum-average range.
modeled_input: Complete 600 Ω transformer-matched midrange EQ with passive filter and valve makeup. Bypass keeps the amplifier in circuit.
published_input_conditions: The original MEQ-5 specifies −10 to +8 dBm optimum average input, and +4 dBm as a practical input allowing peak headroom. The distortion test uses +10 dBm into 600 Ω; +20 dBm is maximum peak OUTPUT. Flat is unity gain.

reference_basis: Channel service alignment produces 0 dB at the insert send from +4 dB at the line connector. Use the insert level as an estimate at EQ input pin 48.
modeled_input: Original SSL 82E242 black-knob channel EQ daughterboard. The electrical boundary runs from pin 48 to pin 43 and omits console line and metering stages.
published_input_conditions: The SSL drawing identifies EQ input and output and the active filter stages. A nominal input or overload voltage at pins 48/43 was not located. Power rails and gain-control ranges do not specify an audio level.

reference_basis: Provisional +4 dBu professional mastering line input. The available circuit is a related 430C drawing.
modeled_input: One mono differential line path of the MES-432C/9 mastering EQ, reconstructed using a related Sontec MES-430C board and MEP-250A controls.
published_input_conditions: The archived audio-board drawing identifies the 430C circuit used in the reconstruction. No factory nominal or maximum for the requested 432C/9 analogue input was found. Hardware gain-step markings express EQ change.

reference_basis: The modeled J11 link selects the documented +4 dBu line input.
modeled_input: ED2162 Rev 8 mono strip, balanced desk line input modeled single-ended, J11 engaged. Ends at channel-fader amplifier, before buses.
published_input_conditions: Soundcraft specifies +4 dBu or −10 dBV line interface via links; the preset selects +4 dBu (1.228 V RMS). The manual separately defines −6 dBu internal operation, including insert points. J11 changes the front-end sensitivity.

reference_basis: Provisional 0 dBu internal EQ reference. Voltage at this specific board input is undocumented.
modeled_input: Part of original type 1038 channel, from C26 at the high-pass amplifier feed through C46 at the midrange amplifier output. External mic and line stages are outside the model.
published_input_conditions: Original Trident ED3001 documents the 1038 circuit. No rating at C26 was found. Trident’s later two-channel A-Range rack specifies +4 dBu nominal and +24 dBu maximum line input at its external transformer-balanced connector.

reference_basis: Provisional 0 dBu internal EQ reference. Voltage at this specific board input is undocumented.
modeled_input: S800 implementation, starting at C4 after the line receiver and ending after the low-cut filter before the balanced output stage.
published_input_conditions: The Cameron/S800 schematic and project drawings document the EQ core. No normal or maximum level at C4 was established. The later Trident two-channel rack is +4 dBu nominal, +24 dBu maximum at the external line input.

reference_basis: Provisional +4 dBu professional line input. The factory maximum of +20 dBm is an overload reference.
modeled_input: Whole mono parametric EQ with one input side grounded; the model includes the line driver and transformer output.
published_input_conditions: The original manual rates maximum input +20 dBm (7.75 V RMS), 40 kΩ balanced or 20 kΩ unbalanced. Output delivers +24 dBm into 600 Ω or +20 dBm into 150 Ω. Boost can overload a filter section before the input itself clips.

reference_basis: Provisional -40 dBu microphone reference with the VP312 input pad off. Do not use a line-level feed as the nominal mic signal.
modeled_input: CAPI VP312-VPR Rev A microphone input, 150 Ω source, pad out, transformer input, output full into 600 Ω. The preset does not model the hardware output fader.
published_input_conditions: CAPI’s Rev A drawing labels a −20 dB pad, input transformer, discrete op amp and output network. It gives no nominal mic signal or explicit maximum input for the build. Original API 312 family gain and output ratings are for a different circuit assembly.

reference_basis: Factory nominal distortion test on the mic input, -40 dB re 0.774 V at 34 dB gain.
modeled_input: 43E241 balanced mic connector to preamp-out patch, before fader, equalizer and bus. Model uses 150 Ω source and switchable pad.
published_input_conditions: MCI’s nominal mic distortion test specifies −40 dBv input (7.74 mV RMS), −6 dBv out, hence 34 dB gain. Its separate high-input test specifies 0 dBv in (0.774 V RMS) and +20 dBv out. MCI expressly references dBv to 0.774 V.

reference_basis: Factory connector drawing, 0 dBu line input. The modeled signal enters before the line transformer.
modeled_input: EH10023 original balanced line input F/H to transformer-balanced output R/T, external K–L link, EQ bypassed and HPF off. This is a line driver path even though the preset is filed under preamps.
published_input_conditions: Neve’s connector drawing labels 0 dBu line in and balanced out (775 mV RMS); unbalanced out is −3 dBu. Line input is 10 kΩ bridging with −10 to +20 dB gain available across the complete hardware selector. Maximum >+26 dBu into 600 Ω belongs to the output.
